Beddows & Company / Hatch Management and Technology Consulting (2000). Minerals & Metals Working Group - Industry Table: Iron & Steel Plant Level Analysis and Options Paper, Final Report. Prepared for the Canadian National Climate Change Process Minerals and Metals Working Group. Report PR72179.002 Rev 3, 10 February 2000.

Region: Canada (plant-level analysis of Algoma, Dofasco, Stelco, IPSCO and Ispat Sidbec, 75% of capacity) plus US co-generation projects used as cost references. Locators are PRINTED page numbers of the form chapter-page (Rev. 3, Page 4-8). The report prints NO specific energy consumption by process and no plant SEC (energy intensity appears only as an unlabeled chart, Fig. 3-7); it is a policy and measures study. Loaded: co-generation (combined cycle) capital costs per kW and scenarios, reheat furnace efficiency package cost per t (incremental), BOF gas recovery and scrap preheating equipment costs, and sector emission figures in _other-values. Measures with savings and payback are in _measures (reheat furnace 15% fuel saving, 4-6 year payback). NPV/payback tables for government incentive measures (ACCA, tax credit, carbon tax; Chapters 5-7) and trade analysis (Chapter 8) are policy analysis and were not loaded. TRAPS: (1) All dollar amounts printed "$" without currency or price year: Canadian dollars assumed except where "US$" is printed; publication year 2000 used. (2) Tables 4-2 and 4-3 print the unit as US$/KWh but mean US$ per kW installed; Gary's Ferry printed 823 US$/kW conflicts with US$170 million/150 MW (1133); Whiting 454 matches the upper end of its US$200-250 million. (3) Capital cost and savings quoted per tonne of steel for reheat furnaces are sector-average estimates over nameplate capacity (10.6 Mt and 6.5 Mt per year), not equipment costs. (4) The two CO2 totals (14.5 Mt on-site, 1996; 17.0 Mt including indirect, 1998) use different boundaries. (5) Co-generation costs are for the whole facility; fuel mix varies (BFG, natural gas, oil), and the 8000 h/yr, $0.04/kWh and 20-year life are assumptions of the study.
